name: Silhouette
summary: A form shown as one solid shape with no inner line, read only from its outer edge.
how: Fill the shape with one colour on a plain ground.
Choose the most typical side view, so that the edge alone names the object.
Cut inner detail as gaps of at least 1/16 of the shape width, not as lines.
Keep the contrast between shape and ground high.

origin.note: Greek vase painters fill figures with black slip and scratch the detail.

adoptions.via: Cut black paper profiles become a fashion in France and take the name of the minister Etienne de Silhouette.
Lotte Reiniger shows The Adventures of Prince Achmed, a feature film of cut paper silhouettes.
Otl Aicher draws the Munich Olympic pictograms as white-on-colour figure silhouettes.
Font Awesome 1.0 gives the web a free set of solid glyphs in an icon font.

sources.title: Lotte Reiniger, Die Abenteuer des Prinzen Achmed (1926)
